turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. I'll use them well.

I'm here about Owen's Hamlet essay. I understand the zero is already in the gradebook. You entered it before you called me.

I'd like to know why.
Owen talks about you in class, by the way.

That's nice. But it isn't why I'm here.

I asked about the zero. You entered it before you called me.

What was your evidence? Besides the checker's score.
He's one of the kindest kids I teach. He walked a new student around the building all through September.

I'm glad. He is kind.

But kindness isn't evidence. Neither is a 94%.

Here's what I need. What tool produced that number? What version? On what date did you run it?

And did you compare the essay to anything Owen wrote in class? Drafts, outlines, in-class writing. With dates.
A kid like that doesn't cheat out of malice. He was overwhelmed. We can both agree on that, right?

No. I won't agree to that.

You've just assumed he cheated. He didn't. He told me he wrote it himself.

So there's no "overwhelmed" to discuss. There's a number from a checker.

Show me something I can verify. The report. The date you ran it. His drafts in the document history.

Until then, I'm not agreeing to anything.
